suggestion: Verify if this column exists in source documents or if data collection was incomplete; dictionary notes 'No Information' for this field

issue: Column 'Disadvantaged' defined in data dictionary but not found in any data file
suggestion: Verify if this column exists in source documents or if data collection was incomplete; dictionary notes 'No Information' for this field

suggestion: Update data dictionary to document these additional columns or clarify if they are for internal use only

issue: Data dictionary specifies PWSID should have 'PA' prepended, but source column is 'PWSID' without documented prefix in column header
suggestion: Clarify in documentation whether 'PA' prefix is added during data processing or if source data already contains it

issue: Column 'Loan (2)' appears to be a duplicate or variant naming of 'Loan' column; inconsistent with other fundable list files
suggestion: Standardize column naming across all fundable list files to use consistent naming convention

issue: pa-sfy26-comprehensive-list-q2.csv has PV RATING as logical type with 100% NA (all missing), but pa-sfy26-comprehensive-list-q1.csv has it as numeric with 5.1% NA. Dictionary specifies this should map to 'Project Score' which should be numeric. Data type mismatch between Q1 and Q2 files violates consistency requirement.
suggestion: Convert PV RATING in Q2 file to numeric type. Investigate source documents for missing PV RATING values in Q2 data and populate where available, or document why Q2 lacks this field.

issue: pa-sfy26-comprehensive-list-q2.csv has LOAN # as numeric with 27.7% NA (18 of 65 missing). pa-sfy26-comprehensive-list-q1.csv has 5.1% NA. According to dictionary, Loan # (Project ID) should be a required field with no missing values. High NA rate in Q2 is problematic.
suggestion: Populate missing LOAN # values in Q2 comprehensive list from source documents or cross-reference with fundable lists. If truly unavailable, document and mark as 'No Information' for downstream expectations.

issue: PROJECT COST is stored as character type (with $ formatting and commas) in comprehensive lists, but needs to be numeric for analysis. Values like '$7,390,224' require parsing.
suggestion: Parse PROJECT COST to remove $ and commas, convert to numeric type for proper financial analysis and constraints checking.

issue: GREEN AMOUNT is stored as character type (formatted with $) in comprehensive lists and as numeric in fundable lists. Inconsistent data types across files.
suggestion: Standardize GREEN AMOUNT to numeric type across all files by removing $ and comma formatting.

field: Categorical Green or Business Case Green
issue: pa-sfy26-ec-fundable-list.csv and pa-sfy26-lslr-fundable-list.csv have this column as logical type with 100% NA. pa-sfy26-base-fundable-list.csv and pa-sfy26-supp-fundable-list.csv have it as character with 50-55.6% NA. Inconsistent types and high missing rates.
suggestion: Verify if this column should contain data. If yes, populate from source documents. If not used, remove or clearly document as intentionally empty for specific fund sources.

issue: pa-sfy26-ec-fundable-list.csv and pa-sfy26-lslr-fundable-list.csv have 'Green' column as logical with 100% NA. pa-sfy26-supp-fundable-list.csv has 'Green' as numeric with 55.6% NA. Dictionary maps to 'Green Amount' but data structure is inconsistent.
suggestion: Clarify whether 'Green' column should contain numeric funding amounts or boolean flags. Standardize type and populate missing values or document intentional absences.

issue: MTGDATE in comprehensive lists has 5.1-6.2% NA values. Dictionary does not specify whether this is a required field. Date format varies (e.g., '10/15/2025' vs '04/08/2026' in fundable lists).
suggestion: Standardize date format across all files (ISO 8601 recommended). Clarify whether MTGDATE is required and populate missing values or document reason for absence.

issue: Dictionary specifies PWSID should have 'PA' prepended, but in comprehensive lists PWSID is numeric without prefix. Fundable lists do not include PWSID column.
suggestion: Prepend 'PA' to PWSID values in comprehensive lists per dictionary specification. Add PWSID to fundable lists if required for standardized dashboard.

issue: pa-sfy26-lslr-fundable-list.csv has LOAN # as character type, while other fundable lists have it as numeric. Dictionary specifies Project ID should be 'concise and unique'.
suggestion: Standardize LOAN # to numeric type across all fundable lists, or standardize to character if loans contain non-numeric identifiers.

field: DEP PROJECT RATING vs PV RATING
issue: Comprehensive lists have 'DEP PROJECT RATING' (numeric) which appears to be different from 'PV RATING' (Project Score per dictionary). Relationship between these two fields is unclear.
suggestion: Clarify which field maps to 'Project Score' in the standardized dashboard. Document whether DEP PROJECT RATING and PV RATING serve different purposes.

issue: pa-sfy26-comprehensive-list-q1.csv has POPULATION range [0, 1600000]. A population of 0 is unrealistic for a water system. May indicate data entry error or placeholder.
suggestion: Review records with POPULATION = 0 to verify accuracy. Consider whether these represent incomplete data entries that should be marked as missing.

issue: 'Small (Cust < 10K)' column uses 'x' to indicate true/NA for false. This is non-standard. High NA rates vary by fundable list (44.4-81.8%).
suggestion: Standardize to boolean (TRUE/FALSE) or 'Yes'/'No' format for consistency. Document missing values in fundable lists.

issue: Fundable lists use 'Loan' or 'Loan (2)' as column names instead of consistent terminology. Unclear what these represent vs 'Total Assistance Amount'.
suggestion: Standardize column naming: clarify whether 'Loan' represents the loan portion (excluding principal forgiveness) or a different metric. Use consistent names across all fundable lists.

issue: REGION is categorical (I-VI) but dictionary does not specify what these codes represent. No mapping provided to actual region names.
suggestion: Document REGION code mapping (e.g., Region I = Northeast, etc.). Consider including region names alongside codes for clarity.

issue: Dictionary notes that applicant name may contain municipality names but does not necessarily indicate project benefit location. Comprehensive lists show high cardinality (64-78 distinct values) with limited standardization.
suggestion: Extract and standardize borrower names separately from geographic references. Cross-reference with PWSID for canonical utility names.

issue: The script overrides 'disinfection byproduct' projects to 'General' type, but the data dictionary explicitly lists 'DBP,' 'disinfection byproduct,' 'HAA5,' 'haloacetic acid,' 'trihalomethane,' and 'THM' as EC keyword triggers. Projects matching these terms should be classified as 'Emerging Contaminants,' not 'General'.
suggestion: Remove or invert the post-hoc mutate that sets project_type to 'General' for 'disinfection byproduct' matches, or confirm with the data dictionary owner that this override is intentional and document the exception.

issue: The variable 'ec_str' is used in the project_type case_when to match EC keywords but is never defined within the script. This will cause a runtime error unless it is defined in the global environment outside this function, which is fragile and undocumented.
suggestion: Define 'ec_str' explicitly inside the function as a regex string containing all EC keywords from the data dictionary (cyanotoxin, dioxane, IIJA EC, IIJA-EC, BIL EC, BIL-EC, emerging containment, emerging contaminant, lithium, manganese, Mn, PFPeA, PFAS, PFOA, PFOS, DBP, disinfection byproduct, HAA5, haloacetic acid, trihalomethane, THM, Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring Rule, Perfluoro-n-pentanoic acid).

issue: The EC keyword list in ec_str (assumed external) may be missing several terms required by the dictionary: 'cyanotoxin', 'dioxane', 'lithium', 'manganese', 'Mn', 'Perfluoro-n-pentanoic acid', 'PFPeA', 'emerging containment', 'Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring Rule'. If ec_str does not include all of these, valid EC projects will be misclassified.
suggestion: Ensure ec_str includes all EC indicator terms listed in the data dictionary verbatim.

issue: The lead keyword check in project_type logic does not exclude instances of 'non-lead' as required by the data dictionary ('Note that any instances of non-lead should not be captured as lead projects'). A project description containing 'non-lead' would still match the grepl for 'lead'.
suggestion: Add a negative lookahead or pre-filter to exclude 'non-lead' matches, e.g., use a regex like '(?<!non-)lead' or explicitly check that 'non-lead' is not present before classifying as Lead.

issue: The data dictionary states that projects on the Q2 Comprehensive List that do not appear in the Q1 Comprehensive List or Fundable Lists should receive 'No Information'. The script uses the flag 'pa_comp_q2_loan_nef' (projects in Q2 but not Q1) for this, but does not separately check whether those projects appear in the Fundable Lists. A project could be in Q2, not in Q1, but present in a Fundable List, and still be incorrectly assigned 'No Information' instead of 'Yes'.
suggestion: Before assigning 'No Information', verify the project is also absent from all Fundable Lists. If present in a Fundable List, expecting_funding should be 'Yes'.

issue: The script derives project_name for comprehensive-list projects by extracting text after the first dash from the applicant field. If applicant_name contains an em-dash or en-dash that was already replaced with a hyphen, the extraction may work, but if the applicant name itself contains hyphens (e.g., hyphenated town names), the extraction will truncate the project name incorrectly.
suggestion: Verify that all applicant_name values use a consistent delimiter and consider using a more robust split strategy, or cross-validate extracted project names against source data.

issue: The borrower field is extracted as text before the first dash in applicant_name or project_name. The data dictionary states borrower is the 'Community water system or municipality receiving the funding,' which may not always be the substring before the first dash, especially for applicants with hyphens in their names.
suggestion: Audit borrower extractions for applicants with hyphenated names to confirm correctness, and add manual overrides where needed.

issue: The data dictionary specifies that Geographic Reference uses CITY and COUNTY columns from the Comprehensive Lists. The script maps this to 'community_served' rather than 'geographic_reference'. While the underlying data source is correct, the output column name does not match the standardized dashboard field name 'Geographic Reference'.
suggestion: Confirm whether the output column should be named 'geographic_reference' per the dashboard standard, or document that 'community_served' is an intentional alias.

issue: Two projects have their loan_number hardcoded via manual case_when overrides (Municipal Authority of the Borough of Waterford and Pittsburgh Water & Sewer Authority). If source data is updated, these hardcoded values may become stale or incorrect.
suggestion: Document the reason for these overrides with source citations, and add a validation check to flag if these project names appear with different loan numbers in future data refreshes.

issue: The script filters out epic_ids 5 and 14 from pa_comp_no_info_project_id with a comment that they are population amendments. Dropping rows may remove valid project records if the comment is incorrect or if source data changes.
suggestion: Add more explicit validation to confirm these rows are truly duplicates or amendments rather than unique projects, and document the source justification for exclusion.

issue: The data dictionary note states PA may include a final placeholder 'project' in Fundable Lists with reserved assistance amounts, which should be excluded. The script has an author comment that there are no such projects, but there is no programmatic check to detect and exclude them if they appear.
suggestion: Add a filter to detect and exclude any fundable list rows where project_name or a key identifier matches a known placeholder pattern (e.g., 'future projects', 'PENNVEST and DEP'), or add a test assertion to confirm no such rows exist.

issue: The pa_fundable_gs and pa_fundable_base tables do not assign project_type at load time (unlike pa_fundable_ec which gets 'Emerging Contaminants' and pa_fundable_lsl which gets 'Lead'). project_type for these is determined later via keyword matching. If project_name or project_description keywords are absent, these may default to 'General' even if they are lead or EC projects.
suggestion: This is consistent with the dictionary logic, but add a QA check to confirm no base or gen supp fundable projects are unexpectedly classified as General when their project name contains lead or EC keywords.

issue: When proj_description is NA, the script sets project_description to 'No Information' and does not append prob_description. However, it is possible that proj_description is NA but prob_description is not, in which case prob_description data is silently lost.
suggestion: Revise the logic to check each field independently and concatenate whichever fields are non-NA, e.g., only skip prob_description concatenation if it is also NA.

issue: The script correctly sets requested_amount to NA (character) per the dictionary's 'No Information' specification, but uses as.character(NA) rather than the string 'No Information' used consistently elsewhere in the script.
suggestion: For consistency with other 'No Information' fields in the script, consider setting requested_amount to the string 'No Information' rather than NA, unless downstream systems distinguish between the two.

issue: The script correctly sets disadvantaged to as.character(NA) per the dictionary's 'No Information' specification, but similarly uses NA rather than the string 'No Information'. Same inconsistency as requested_amount.
suggestion: Use the string 'No Information' for consistency with other fields, or ensure downstream processing treats NA and 'No Information' equivalently.

issue: The 'list' column is retained in the final dplyr::select output but is not defined as a field in the data dictionary. This is likely an internal tracking column, which is acceptable, but should be documented.
suggestion: Document that 'list' is an internal provenance column not part of the standardized dashboard schema.

issue: 'state' and 'state_fiscal_year' are hardcoded as 'Pennsylvania' and '2026' respectively. These are not defined in the data dictionary as standard fields but appear in the select statement. This is acceptable for pipeline use but should be documented.
suggestion: Document these as pipeline metadata fields added beyond the standard data dictionary schema.

issue: The EC fundable list has a column named 'Loan (2)' (with parentheses and a space), which after janitor::clean_names() becomes 'loan_2'. The script renames 'loan_2' to 'loan'. However, the base and supplemental fundable lists have a column named 'Loan' (no number), which after clean_names() becomes 'loan'. The LSLR fundable list also has 'Loan (2)' → 'loan_2', but the LSLR processing block does NOT rename loan_2 to loan before the bind_rows. This means pa_fundable_lsl will have a 'loan_2' column rather than 'loan', causing misalignment in bind_rows and the subsequent select() call which expects 'loan'.
suggestion: Add dplyr::rename(loan = loan_2) to the pa_fundable_lsl mutate/rename pipeline, mirroring what is done for pa_fundable_ec.

issue: In the LSLR fundable list, the 'Loan #' column is of character type (e.g., '80327', '80326', 'Pending'), while in all other fundable lists it is numeric. When fread reads it with colClasses='character' this is fine, but clean_names() will produce 'loan_number'. The hardcoded case_when fix for loan_number=='Pending' → 'No Information' should work, but only if 'Pending' is the exact string. If the source has whitespace variants (e.g., ' Pending'), trimws is not applied before this check and it would silently fail to convert.
suggestion: Apply trimws() to loan_number before the ifelse(loan_number == 'Pending', ...) check in pa_fundable mutate step.

issue: The Q2 comprehensive list's 'PV RATING' column is 100% NA (logical type per column summary). After clean_names() it becomes 'pv_rating'. The script calls clean_numeric_string(pv_rating) which will operate on an entirely NA logical vector. Depending on clean_numeric_string's implementation, this may error or return all 'No Information'. More critically, since the Q2 list is preferred over Q1, all projects sourced from Q2 will have 'No Information' project_score even where Q1 had valid scores.
suggestion: After merging Q1 and Q2, coalesce pv_rating from Q1 for projects that appear in both lists before computing project_score, so valid Q1 scores are not lost for shared projects.

issue: The Q1 comprehensive list contains 'MERCERSBURG WATER AUTHORITY – WATER SYSTEM IMPROVEMENTS, PHASE 2' with a Unicode en-dash (U+2013). The script applies str_replace_all to replace en/em-dashes with hyphens in applicant_name, but this replacement happens AFTER project_name is derived via str_extract(applicant, '(?<=-).*'), which extracts text after a hyphen. If applicant_name still contains the en-dash at extraction time, the lookbehind '(?<=-)' won't match the en-dash and project_name will be NA for that row.
suggestion: Move the en/em-dash replacement on applicant_name (and applicant) to before the project_name extraction step, or include \u2013 and \u2014 in the lookbehind pattern used for project_name.

field: borrower extraction regex for fundable-only rows
issue: For rows where applicant_name is NA (fundable list rows not matched to comprehensive), borrower is extracted from project_name using '^[^\-\u2013\u2014]+'. EC fundable project names include entries like 'Aqua Pennsylvania Inc. - Cabot/Hall Rd PFAS Project PWSID PA1460073'. The regex correctly stops at the hyphen. However, 'Pittsburgh Water & Sewer Authority -  2026B LSLR' (from LSLR list) has a double space before '2026B'. The borrower extraction itself is fine here, but the applicant str_to_title conversion won't apply since applicant_name is NA. Borrower will be title-cased from project_name correctly only if the ec_str and project_name are consistent — but 'Aqua Pennsylvania Inc.' (no comma) in EC list vs 'Aqua Pennsylvania, Inc.' in LSLR list may cause different borrower strings for the same entity.
suggestion: Normalize entity name punctuation (e.g., 'Inc.' vs 'Inc') in a post-processing step, or document the inconsistency as a known data quality issue.

field: project_type classification — 'lead-lag' and 'one lead and one lag' exceptions
issue: The script has special-case overrides to classify 'lead-lag' or 'one lead and one lag' descriptions as 'Emerging Contaminants' rather than 'Lead'. These strings are checked before the general lead regex. However, if a description contains 'lead-lag' AND also contains 'PFAS' or another EC keyword, it would be caught by the lead-lag exception and classified as EC — which may or may not be correct. More importantly, descriptions containing 'non-lead' are not explicitly excluded from the lead regex match per the data dictionary guidance, only the note in the dictionary mentions it; the script does not have a 'non-lead' exclusion guard.
suggestion: Add a negative lookahead or prior case_when branch to explicitly handle 'non-lead' so those are not classified as Lead, as instructed by the data dictionary.

issue: For rows sourced from fundable lists (grepl('fundable', list)), project_name is kept as-is from the fundable list project_name column. For EC fundable rows, one project name is 'Aqua Pennsylvania Inc. - Cabot/Hall Rd PFAS Project PWSID PA1460073' — this embeds a PWSID in the project name. This will appear in the dashboard's project_name field verbatim, which is noisy and inconsistent with how other project names appear.
suggestion: Strip the trailing 'PWSID PA...' suffix from project_name for EC fundable rows, e.g., using str_remove(project_name, '\\s*PWSID\\s*PA\\d+$').

issue: PWSID is read as numeric (range 1090046–7380035), so leading zeros are dropped before 'PA' is prepended. For example, a PWSID stored as 1090046 becomes 'PA1090046' (7 digits), which is correct for PA PWSIDs. However, if any PWSID has fewer than 7 digits after numeric parsing (e.g., a value like 90046 that should be 0090046), the prepended 'PA' would yield an incorrect ID. The colClasses='character' argument should prevent numeric parsing, but fread may still interpret the column as numeric if all values look numeric.
suggestion: Explicitly set the PWSID column to character in colClasses or verify post-load that all PWSIDs have exactly 7 digits after the 'PA' prefix.

issue: Date formats are inconsistent across files: base and Q1/Q2 use 'M/D/YYYY' (e.g., '7/16/2026'), supp uses zero-padded 'MM/DD/YYYY' (e.g., '01/12/2026'), and LSLR uses mixed formats including '04/08/2026' and '1/15/2027'. The script does not parse or use this column, so no breakage occurs — but if it is ever used downstream, the mixed formats will require handling.
suggestion: If the binding commitment date is used in future processing, apply a date parser tolerant of both formats (e.g., lubridate::mdy()).

issue: City values in the source data are all-caps (e.g., 'PITTSBURGH', 'MERCERBURG'). str_to_title will convert 'PITTSBURGH' to 'Pittsburgh' correctly. However, multi-word all-caps cities or counties with abbreviations (e.g., 'MCMURRAY') will become 'Mcmurray' rather than 'McMurray'. Also, the sample shows 'MERCERBURG' (missing an 's') which is a data entry error that will be preserved verbatim.
suggestion: Consider a lookup table for known city/county name corrections, and document that str_to_title may not properly capitalize abbreviations.

field: project_description construction when prob_description is NA
issue: The script builds project_description as paste0('Project Description: ', proj_description, '; Problem Description: ', prob_description). If proj_description is not NA but prob_description IS NA, the output will be 'Project Description: <text>; Problem Description: NA' — the literal string 'NA' will appear in the output rather than being omitted or replaced.
suggestion: Replace NA in prob_description with empty string or 'No Information' before the paste0, e.g., replace_na(prob_description, 'No Information').

issue: The Q1 comprehensive list shows population range=[0, 1600000], meaning at least one row has population=0. After clean_numeric_string this will likely become '0' (not 'No Information'). A population of 0 is likely a data entry error or placeholder and may cause issues in downstream analysis.
suggestion: Add a check to convert population values of 0 to 'No Information' or flag them for review.

issue: The script filters out epic_ids 5 and 14 as known population amendment duplicates. This hardcoded filter is brittle — if rows are added or reordered in the source data, the row_number()-based epic_id assignment will shift, causing the wrong rows to be excluded or the correct amendment rows to be included.
suggestion: Instead of filtering by row number/epic_id, identify amendment rows by a stable characteristic (e.g., matching PWSID + applicant_name combination) to make deduplication robust to row order changes.

issue: The select() call on pa_fundable includes 'loan' as a column. For EC and LSLR lists, 'loan' comes from renaming 'loan_2' (Loan (2) column). For base and supp lists, 'loan' comes directly from the 'Loan' column. If the LSLR rename issue (see ERROR above) is fixed, this will be consistent. If not fixed, the select() will error because 'loan' won't exist in pa_fundable_lsl.
suggestion: Confirm all four fundable list data frames have a 'loan' column before the bind_rows and select() operations.

issue: The hardcoded case_when overrides for Waterford and Pittsburgh Water & Sewer Authority set loan_number to '82266' and '80330' as character strings. clean_numeric_string will then process these. If clean_numeric_string strips non-numeric characters, these pure-numeric strings will pass through correctly. No issue expected, but should be verified against the actual clean_numeric_string implementation.
suggestion: Verify clean_numeric_string handles plain numeric strings without modification.

field: APPLICANT NAME — extra internal space in Q2 data
issue: The Q2 comprehensive list shows 'PITTSBURGH WATER & SEWER AUTHORITY -  2026B LSLR' with two spaces before '2026B'. After str_to_title and str_extract for project_name ('(?<=-).*'), the extracted project_name will be '  2026B LSLR' with leading spaces. trimws is applied to borrower but the project_name extraction uses trimws only on the borrower, not on the right side of the dash for project_name.
suggestion: Apply trimws() or str_squish() to the extracted project_name value when it is derived from applicant via the regex lookbehind.
